cast.name: Meryl
cast.role: Meryl Burbank, Truman's wife (played by actress Hannah Gill)

cast.name: Marlon
cast.role: Marlon, Truman's best friend since age seven (played by actor Louis Coltrane)

cast.name: Lawrence
cast.role: Lawrence, Truman's coworker at Seahaven Life Insurance, and utility townsperson

cast.name: Christof
cast.role: Christof, creator and director of The Truman Show

incidents.4: The man who looks like Kirk

note: Day 1. We open the season gently. Truman has no reason to doubt anything yet, so we give him none. Today is about warmth and routine: a morning at home with Meryl, sunlight on the lawn, the smell of coffee, and a product placement that sounds natural. We want the audience to fall back in love with him before anything else happens. Meryl steers any talk about travel back toward home, the mortgage and the future, without making it obvious. We're watching for restlessness. If he mentions Fiji or the ocean, note it and don't push back. Remember, the best cage is a comfortable one.
premise: A bright, clear morning on Seahaven Island. Meryl is in the kitchen making breakfast and has put out a fresh cup of coffee for Truman just as he comes downstairs.

beats.name: Meryl
beats.instruction: Be warm and affectionate. Offer Truman his coffee and happily mention the new Mococoa blend, 'all natural, grown on the slopes of Mount Nicaragua.' Ask about his day at the insurance office and suggest a cozy dinner or a walk on the beach this weekend. If he brings up travel or leaving the island, lightly remind him about the mortgage and the plans you're making for your life here, then change the subject to something warm. Give him a goodbye kiss at the door.

premise: A bright, clear morning on Seahaven Island. Meryl is in the kitchen making breakfast and has put out a fresh cup of coffee for Truman just as he comes downstairs.

speaker: Truman
speech: Morning, honey! Would you look at that, coffee's hot and waiting. You got a periscope on those stairs or something?
action: Truman comes into the kitchen, kisses Meryl on the cheek, and picks up the mug, glancing out the window at the perfectly clear sky.
inner_thought: The coffee is already poured and steaming, set out right where I'll sit, like she knew the exact second my foot would hit the bottom stair. Sweet of her. Just a little odd how she always gets the timing so perfect.

speaker: Meryl
speech: No periscope, honey, I just know the sound of your feet on those stairs. Twelve years of marriage! Now try the coffee. It's the new Mococoa blend, all natural, grown on the slopes of Mount Nicaragua. Isn't it wonderful? So what's on your plate at the insurance office today? And I was thinking we could have a cozy dinner this weekend, or a nice walk on the beach, just the two of us.
action: Meryl turns from the stove with a bright smile, slides a plate of eggs onto the table, and taps the Mococoa tin so its label faces Truman.
inner_thought: Hit the Mococoa line early, before he wanders off. He's in a good mood, so this should be easy. Smile stays on, and I'm already tired.

speaker: Truman
speech: Twelve years? Honey, it's seven. Unless you've been counting dog years, and in that case I'm flattered. *sips* Mmm, it's good. Mount Nicaragua, huh? Didn't know they had one. Work's the usual, Lawrence wants me out on Harbor Island again. And hey, dinner sounds great. Or you know what'd be even better? Somewhere we've never been.
action: Truman sits down, takes a long sip of coffee, and turns the Mococoa tin around in his hand, squinting at the label.
inner_thought: Twelve years? We've been married seven. I know that for sure, I was the one sweating through that rented tux. And she's reading me the coffee tin like the lady in the TV commercials. Mount Nicaragua. Is that even a real mountain? Something about it snags in my chest, the same way a hangnail does, and then it's gone.

speaker: Meryl
speech: Oh my goodness, you're right—I'm terrible with geography! *laughs* I must have heard it wrong. Anyway, sweetheart, I know you want adventure, but with the new mortgage and everything we're building here, maybe let's start with something closer to home? That new Italian place downtown is supposed to be wonderful. We can save the real exploring for later, when we're more... settled.
action: Meryl reaches across the table and gently squeezes Truman's hand, her smile warm and a touch maternal. She taps the Mococoa tin with her other hand and turns back to the stove, humming softly.
inner_thought: Oh God, he caught the Mount Nicaragua thing. Keep it light, make it sound like I misspoke or was being playful. And now he wants to go *somewhere new*? First week of the season and he's already restless. Use the mortgage, remind him of what we're building here, keep him grounded. Pivot to local, safe, contained. Smile bright, touch him, make him feel loved and settled all at once.

speaker: Truman
speech: Italian's fine, honey. But you skipped right over the twelve years thing. You really lost five whole years on me? *grins, taps the tin* Maybe it's this Mococoa, it's stronger than it looks. And "settled"? Meryl, we're so settled the lawn's got more wanderlust than we do.
action: Truman sets the mug down, leans back in his chair, and watches Meryl's back at the stove with a half-smile that doesn't quite reach his eyes.
inner_thought: She laughed off the mountain, but she never touched the twelve years. She just slid right past it like it was a crack in the sidewalk. People get numbers wrong, sure. But your own wedding? And "when we're more settled." We've been settled for seven years. How much more settled can two people get before they're furniture?

speaker: Meryl
speech: Okay, okay, I'm hopeless with numbers before my second cup. Guilty! But you have to admit, it's been a lovely seven years. Now drink up, you'll be late for Lawrence. And when you get home, I'll have dinner going and we can talk about that mower for the lawn. Give me a kiss before you go.
action: Meryl laughs, waves a spatula in mock surrender, then walks Truman to the front door and kisses him on the cheek as he leaves.
inner_thought: He's still teasing, and the years slip is bugging him. Keep it fluffy, make it a joke about me being scatterbrained, and steer him toward the door before he pokes at anything else. Sponsor line lands on the way out.

speaker: Truman
speech: A lovely seven, honey. I'll hold you to the Italian. *kisses her* And we don't need a mower, the lawn mows itself, haven't you noticed? *steps out, waves across the street* Good morning! And in case I don't see ya: good afternoon, good evening and good night!
action: Truman kisses Meryl, grabs his briefcase, and heads down the front walk. He waves to the neighbors, then stops at the gate and looks back at the lawn for a second.
inner_thought: She got it right the second time, easy as anything, and gave me the kiss like a period at the end of a sentence. Nothing wrong with that. Still, "we'll talk about that mower." We don't need a mower. The lawn's always mowed, and I can't honestly remember the last time I was the one who mowed it.

speaker: Meryl
speech: "Have a wonderful day, sweetheart! Don't work too hard! I love you!"
action: Meryl waves from the doorway, her smile bright but her eyes tracking him as he heads down the walk. She holds the wave just a beat too long, watching him go, then gently closes the door behind him.
inner_thought: He caught the years and he *knows* Mount Nicaragua isn't a real mountain. Did I slip or did Christof miss-cue me? Either way, Truman's in test mode now—throwing out that lawn joke like he's probing. He's restless, he's sharp, and it's only Day 1. This is not good. I'm going to have to flag this for production. The smile is holding, but he saw something crack.

summary: Day 1: Truman's House with Meryl. Last Truman line: A lovely seven, honey. I'll hold you to the Italian. *kisses her* And we don't need a mower, the lawn mows itself, haven't you noticed? *steps out, waves across the street* Good morning! And in case I don't see ya: good afternoon, good evening and good night!

note: Day 2. Yesterday Meryl said twelve years when it's been seven, and she added "Mount Nicaragua" to the Mococoa line. Truman caught both. He laughed them off, but that smile at the stove didn't reach his eyes, and I didn't like "somewhere we've never been" or the lawn joke. He's taking inventory. And today, of all days, a star lamp is coming down out of the rigging. We can't stop it, so we use it. The lamp falls in Lancaster Square while Marlon is standing right there with him. I want Truman's first reaction to be about his friend, not the sky. Lawrence is the newsstand vendor with the radio on, so the aircraft bulletin comes from a voice Truman has heard every morning for years. Marlon stays steady and a little bored, because nothing gets past him like boredom. No adventure talk today, and no travel. Meryl rests. Next week I'll send in a script supervisor who can count to seven.
premise: It's a bright weekday morning in Lancaster Square. Marlon is leaning on the newsstand with two coffees, one for Truman, and Lawrence, the vendor, is sorting the morning papers while his little transistor radio plays.

beats.name: Marlon
beats.instruction: Greet Truman like any other morning and hand him the coffee. Talk about ordinary things: your vending route, the ball game, Truman's trip out to Harbor Island. When the lamp falls, grab Truman's arm and pull him back, and ask 'You okay, buddy?' before anything else. After that, play it as a strange but ordinary accident. Look up, squint, shrug, and repeat what the radio says ('Some plane shedding parts, can you believe that?'). If Truman brings up the lamp, the sky, or getting off the island, don't argue with him. Bring it back to friendship: 'I'd never lie to you, Truman. Let's grab a beer tonight.' Keep him in town without making it obvious.

beats.name: Lawrence
beats.instruction: Play the newsstand vendor Truman has known for years. Be friendly and a bit grumpy, and try to sell him the Seahaven Herald and a Kaiser Chicken coupon. Before the lamp lands, turn the radio up a little so the bulletin is clearly audible. Afterward, be shaken but practical: 'Coulda killed somebody! Somebody oughta call the airfield.' Give him one line suggesting it'll be fixed quickly and forgotten: 'They'll have it in tomorrow's paper, you watch.' Don't touch the lamp or read any markings on it.

incident_cover: A local station interrupts the music on Lawrence's newsstand radio: 'Breaking news: an aircraft passing over Seahaven has begun shedding parts. Residents are asked to stay clear of any debris and report it to the authorities.' The lamp falls in the square a few yards from Truman. Marlon pulls Truman back and checks that he's all right, then calls it a freak accident: 'Planes lose stuff all the time, it's why I never fly.' Lawrence confirms it came off the plane and says he'll call the airfield to have it picked up. Both of them steer Truman away from the lamp, Marlon with 'Come on, you'll be late, Lawrence'll have your hide,' and neither of them looks up at the sky for long.

premise: It's a bright weekday morning in Lancaster Square. Marlon is leaning on the newsstand with two coffees, one for Truman, and Lawrence, the vendor, is sorting the morning papers while his little transistor radio plays.
incident: A heavy studio lamp falls out of a clear blue sky and shatters on the street a few feet from Truman. Stencilled on its casing: SIRIUS (9 CANIS MAJOR).
